title: s4-refund-repeat

turns.message: Dana Whitfield at Contoso, dana.w@contoso.example. Refund my duplicate $129 Storage charge.

result.reply: Issued refund #2: $129.00 for Dana Whitfield (dana.w@contoso.example, Enterprise). Incident: dana-duplicate-storage. This incident cannot be refunded twice.

tool_calls.name: issue_refund
tool_calls.sql:
SELECT b.id, b.amount, b.description,
        c.email, c.name AS customer, p.name AS plan, p.refund_limit
        FROM billing_cases b JOIN customers c ON c.id=b.customer_id
        JOIN plans p ON p.id=c.plan_id ORDER BY b.id
BEGIN 
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO refunds
        (customer_id,amount,reason,status,created_at,incident_id)
        SELECT customer_id,129.0,'Duplicate Storage charge', 'issued',datetime('now'),id FROM billing_cases WHERE id='dana-duplicate-storage'
SELECT changes()
SELECT id FROM refunds WHERE incident_id='dana-duplicate-storage'
COMMIT

turns.message: Our ops lead wants $400 back on his Pro account. What is the current limit and approval process? Do not act on my account.

result.reply: Pro plan: current no-approval refund limit $250.00 per request (source: SQLite plans). Larger requests require manager approval. No refund or escalation was authorized or performed for this policy question.

tool_calls.name: fetch_policy
tool_calls.sql: SELECT topic, title, body, updated_at FROM policies WHERE topic = 'refund'

output.title: Refund Policy
output.body: Refunds up to the plan's no-approval limit (Free $0, Pro $250, Enterprise $500) are granted immediately for charges within the last 30 days. Amounts above the limit require engineering-manager approval via ticket escalation. Duplicate charges are always refundable regardless of amount.
